skill: i want to learn how to start a minecraft server

route.title: Pick Your Server Type
route.summary: Learn what kind of Minecraft server you want to run. There are three main types: Vanilla (regular Minecraft), Paper (faster and lets you add plugins), and Modded (with mods like dragons or machines). Each works differently.

challenge.prompt: Write which server type you want to start with (Vanilla, Paper, or Modded) and explain in 2-3 sentences why that type sounds coolest to you.

route.title: Download Java
route.summary: Minecraft servers run on Java, which is a programming language. You need to install it on your computer before your server can work. It's free and takes about 5 minutes.

challenge.prompt: Install Java from java.com (get Java 17 or newer). Open your command prompt or terminal, type 'java -version' and take a screenshot showing Java is installed.

route.title: Get Your Server File
route.summary: Download the actual server software. For Vanilla, get it from minecraft.net. For Paper, get it from papermc.io. This is a .jar file that runs your whole server.

challenge.prompt: Download your server .jar file and put it in a new folder called 'MyMinecraftServer'. Take a screenshot of that folder showing the server file inside.

route.title: Start Your Server for the First Time
route.summary: Run the server file using a command. It will create a bunch of files and folders, then stop. This is normal! You need to agree to Minecraft's rules before it runs for real.

challenge.prompt: Open command prompt or terminal in your server folder. Run 'java -jar server.jar' (use your actual filename). Take a screenshot showing it created an eula.txt file and other folders.

route.title: Accept the EULA and Launch
route.summary: Open eula.txt in Notepad or any text editor. Change 'eula=false' to 'eula=true'. This means you agree to Minecraft's End User License Agreement. Save it, then start the server again.

challenge.prompt: Change eula=false to eula=true, save the file, then run your server again. Take a screenshot showing the server console saying 'Done!' and that it's running on port 25565.

route.title: Join Your Own Server
route.summary: Open Minecraft and connect to your server using 'localhost' as the server address. This is a special word that means 'my own computer'. Walk around, break some blocks, and place some blocks to test it.

challenge.prompt: Join your server in Minecraft, build a small 5-block tall tower, and take a screenshot showing you're connected and your tower is there.

route.title: Customize Your Server Settings
route.summary: Open server.properties in a text editor. This file controls everything: game mode, difficulty, whether monsters spawn, how many players can join, the world seed, and more. Each line is one setting.

challenge.prompt: Change at least 3 settings in server.properties (like difficulty, gamemode, or max-players). Write down which 3 settings you changed and what you changed them to, then explain what each one does.

route.title: Learn Basic Server Commands
route.summary: Server operators (ops) can use special commands. Type commands in the server console or in-game with a slash. Important ones: /op [name] makes someone an admin, /gamemode, /time set, /weather, /tp, and /give.

challenge.prompt: Make yourself an op by typing 'op [your username]' in the server console. Then use at least 3 different commands in-game like changing time, weather, or giving yourself an item. Screenshot your chat showing the commands worked.

route.title: Let a Friend Join from Your Network
route.summary: Friends on the same WiFi can join using your local IP address instead of localhost. Find your IP by typing 'ipconfig' (Windows) or 'ifconfig' (Mac) in terminal. Look for something like 192.168.1.X.

challenge.prompt: Find your local IP address and write it down. Then explain in 2-3 sentences how a friend on your WiFi would join your server. If you actually had a friend test it, describe what happened.

route.title: Set Up Port Forwarding
route.summary: For friends outside your house to join, you need port forwarding. This tells your router to let Minecraft traffic through. You log into your router settings and forward port 25565 to your computer's local IP. Every router is different.

challenge.prompt: Research how to port forward for YOUR specific router (look up your router model). Write step-by-step instructions for how you would do it, including what IP and port number you'd use. You don't have to actually do it yet if your parents haven't said it's okay.

route.title: Install Your First Plugin or Mod
route.summary: If you're running Paper, you can add plugins by dropping .jar files in the plugins folder. If you're running Forge or Fabric, you add mods to the mods folder. Restart the server after adding anything new.

challenge.prompt: Download and install one plugin (like EssentialsX for Paper) or one mod (like JEI for modded servers). Start your server and take a screenshot proving the plugin or mod loaded successfully in the server console.

route.title: Build a Spawn Area for Your Server
route.summary: Create a cool spawn point where players first appear. Make it welcoming with signs explaining rules, a starter chest with basic items, and some buildings or decorations. Use /setworldspawn to set the exact spot.

challenge.prompt: Type 'summit' to finish the climb and show your completed Minecraft server journey.
